name: Quebec: language of work and francization of businesses
name_fr: Québec : langue du travail et francisation des entreprises
description: Workers in Quebec have a right to carry out their activities in French; all businesses operating in Quebec, including federally regulated ones, must respect language-of-work obligations. Businesses with 25 or more employees must register with the OQLF for francization.

attributes.jurisdiction: Quebec (applies to employers in Quebec, provincial and federal jurisdiction)

milestones.2023-06-01: Businesses with 5–49 employees must declare to the enterprise register the share of staff who cannot communicate in French
milestones.2025-06-01: Businesses with 25–49 employees must register with the OQLF to begin francization (previously 50+)

attributes.worker_right: Fundamental right to carry out activities in French (OQLF).
attributes.requiring_other_languages: The Charter restricts when an employer may require knowledge of a language other than French; the OQLF conditions were not read in this pass.
attributes.practical_effect: French is the default workplace language; English-only roles exist but employers must justify an English requirement. French ability affects employability in Quebec far more than elsewhere.
attributes.status_dependency: Matters only if Quebec is in scope (USER-PROFILE.md: 'English-only vs bilingual environment' unknown) and depends on the user's status and French ability (unknown).
